title: Buying Cold Medicine at the Pharmacy
situation: You catch a cold and go to a 약국 to describe your symptoms and buy over-the-counter medicine.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Welcome. What's bothering you?
lines.note: 어디가 안 좋으세요 = a softer, common way to ask what's wrong

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I've felt a cold coming on since yesterday.
lines.note: 감기 기운 = signs/onset of a cold, a very natural phrase

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.ko: 증상이 어떻게 되세요? 콧물이나 기침 있으세요?
lines.en: What are your symptoms? Do you have a runny nose or a cough?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I have a runny nose and my throat feels a bit scratchy.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: What about a fever? Do you have one too?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: No fever, but I feel a bit chilly and shivery.
lines.note: 으슬으슬하다 = the chilly, shivery feeling of a cold

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.ko: 그럼 종합감기약 드릴게요. 졸린 성분이 들어 있어요.
lines.en: Then I'll give you a combination cold medicine. It has a drowsy ingredient in it.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How many times a day do I take it?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Take it three times a day, 30 minutes after meals.
lines.note: 식후 30분 = 30 minutes after eating, the standard dosing line

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is it okay to drive after taking this?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: It may make you drowsy, so avoid driving.
lines.note: ~(으)니까 = because/so; gives a reason before advice

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Got it. How much is it?

tip: For colds, fevers, and minor pain you can buy medicine straight from a 약국 without a prescription. Just describe your 증상 (symptoms) clearly. For most antibiotics you'll need a doctor's prescription (처방전) first.

title: Registering at a Clinic Front Desk
situation: You arrive at a 의원 (clinic) for the first time and check in at the front desk before seeing the doctor.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Hello. Let me help you check in. Is this your first visit?
lines.note: 접수 = registration/check-in; 처음 오셨어요 asks if you're a new patient

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, it's my first time.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 그럼 이 문진표 좀 작성해 주세요. 신분증 있으세요?
lines.en: Then please fill out this form. Do you have an ID?
lines.note: 문진표 작성하다 = to fill out a medical questionnaire; 신분증 = ID card

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is an Alien Registration Card okay too?
lines.note: 외국인등록증 = ARC, the ID foreigners carry in Korea

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's fine. Do you have health insurance?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I have insurance through my job.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What are you here to see the doctor about?
lines.note: 어디가 불편하세요 = a polite, standard way to ask your reason for visiting

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I've had a cough that won't stop for a few days.
lines.note: 며칠째 = for several days now; ~아서/어서요 trails off to give a reason

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 알겠습니다. 저쪽에서 잠시만 기다려 주세요. 성함 부를게요.
lines.en: Got it. Please wait over there for a moment. I'll call your name.
lines.note: 성함 = honorific for 'name'; 부르다 = to call

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, do I pay the consultation fee after I'm done?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.ko: 네, 진료 끝나고 여기서 수납하시면 돼요.
lines.en: Yes, you can settle the payment here after your consultation.
lines.note: 수납하다 = to pay/settle the bill, common at clinic desks

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. I'll wait.

tip: First-time patients fill out a short 문진표 (medical questionnaire) and show ID (your 외국인등록증 works). If you're enrolled in 건강보험, clinic visits are cheap. You usually see the doctor first and pay (수납) at the desk on your way out, then take any 처방전 to a nearby pharmacy.
